evidence.claim: Execution of a large-scale cloud-based FWI seismic processing workflow for Petrobras utilizing S-Cube's cloud-native XWI solution on AWS Graviton, as documented on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Industries Blog.

evidence.claim: A formal case study and testimonial from Petrobras (via Geophysical Advisor Gustavo Catão Alves), published by Amazon Web Services (AWS), confirms the successful deployment of S-Cube's cloud-native XWI software and SCC infrastructure to process a 3.3 TB ocean-bottom node seismic dataset from Brazil's Santos Basin, achieving high-fidelity elastic and acoustic FWI results while optimizing operational flexibility.

A joint R&D project and relinquishment report submitted to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate by Wintershall Dea documents that S-Cube's three-stage FWI workflow (AWI, RWI, and true-amplitude FWI) was successfully used to process unprocessed field data from the Norwegian Sea (Licence PL 1129), effectively building velocity models through challenging basalt layers and improving signal-to-noise ratio and event continuity in Kirchhoff and RTM depth migrations.

evidence.claim: SolidGround actively provides quantitative interpretation (QI) of 3D Ultra-High-Resolution Seismic (UHRS) data for massive infrastructure developments, such as delivering UHR3D pre-stack inversion workflows for FEED activities at the Green Volt floating wind project (developed by Flotation Energy and Vårgrønn).

SolidGround partnered in the WINDFARM research project (launched in January 2024 and running through 2026) alongside the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS) and Qeye, funded by Denmark's Energy Technology Development and Demonstration Programme (EUDP) to mature probabilistic and deterministic UHRS inversion methods.

Global Market Standing & Reputation.assessed_on: SolidGround's standing rests on its UHR3D pre-stack inversion work for the Green Volt floating wind project with Flotation Energy and Vårgrønn, and its EUDP-funded WINDFARM project.
